purpose: Primary-system evaluation design for a 20–30 second public video with global context plus local temporal bursts. It must not spread 16 frames across the full duration and call the result dense temporal evidence.

source_requirements.selection: Inspect source video without opening action labels. Freeze a human-observable action sequence and its before/after context before inference. If labels for a candidate were previously opened, it is development-only and cannot be called held out.

local_windows.purpose: temporally observable actions; each window must retain ordered exact source PTS and no repeated decoded frame

input_plan.views: Full frame is required. A hand-object crop is optional only as an additional separately logged view after source inspection establishes the same contact/motion; it must never replace global context.

frozen_pre_inference_checks: Archive global and local exact-native-input contact sheets for human review.
Record decoder frame hashes, source PTS, ordering, native tensor shape/grid, token budget, processor contract, and resource usage.
Prove unique dense local frames and preserve no-reuse checks.
Use the same frozen evidence prompt and model configuration for every planned presentation.

evaluation_after_outputs.review_order: First evaluate source-observable event sequence and order, abstention, schema failures, and unsupported visual claims. Only then open predeclared references if the source remains uncontaminated.
prohibitions: no prompt/model tuning on the test
no general accuracy claim from one source

capability_gate: If a prior dense source-observable diagnostic shows the installed model cannot support a directly visible transition, do not repeat that short diagnostic. A primary-system run needs explicit authorization and must be reported as system-context evidence, not as a rescue of the local action-recognition capability.
